Open installed PWA after removing it from recent apps
OnePlus Nord 4; installed PWA; valid manager session; release build; Wi-Fi.

Remove the app from recent apps. Start screen recording. Tap the home-screen icon and stop timing when dashboard data and actions are usable. Repeat five times without clearing site data. Record every result, median, slowest run, build, OS, Chrome version and network.

Correct signed-in dashboard opens without a blank or repeated loading screen. Compare with the recorded four-second symptom and the previous release under the same conditions. Record the agreed launch budget before assigning pass/fail.
Open PWA after Android has discarded the background process
OnePlus Nord 4; installed PWA; valid session; app unused long enough for Android to discard it.
Record idle duration and battery settings. Open the PWA and time until dashboard data and actions are usable. Repeat after a normal short background interval and record both sets of results.
Long idle and short background resume
Session restores correctly and the page becomes usable without duplicate redirects or stale staff data. Compare timings with the same device and previous release using a documented budget.
Compare first and repeat navigation through core app pages
Release build; manager account with representative rotas and attendance; OnePlus Nord 4.

Navigate Dashboard > Open rotas > a populated rota > Time tracking > Timesheets > Dashboard. Time each page until its main content is usable. Repeat the sequence five times on Wi-Fi and mobile data. Record first visits separately from repeats.
Normal 40-employee location; same account and dataset for comparison

Correct content appears on every route without a full app restart or persistent loading state. First and repeat timings meet the documented per-page budgets with no regression against the previous build.
Direct dashboard load hydrates without replacing server-rendered content
Production release build; manager session; browser console and network panel open.
Open /app/<workspaceSlug>/dashboard directly, refresh five times, then navigate away and back. Watch the initial content, console and network requests.
No React hydration mismatch, client remount flash, duplicate team list, or repeated initial dashboard data load occurs. Dashboard controls work after hydration.
Cold navigation reuses the service-worker preload response
Release build; active service worker; browser supports navigation preload; request recording available.
Close the PWA, reopen a protected route and capture its document requests. Verify navigation preload is enabled and the page renders from that response. Repeat after a service-worker update.
One navigation supplies the document without a second service-worker fetch for the same navigation. Authentication and redirects remain correct.
Navigation works when preload is absent or fails
Isolated browser test with preload unsupported or rejected; installed service worker.
Run a navigation with preload unavailable, then with its promise rejected. Repeat while offline and reconnect afterwards.
Online navigation falls back to the normal fetch. Failed offline navigation shows the offline page. Reconnection restores access without a blank app or cached private HTML.
Keep all manager actions on one row at narrow mobile widths
Manager with rota creation permission; attendance enabled; latest layout change deployed.
At 320, 348, 360 and 390 CSS pixels, open the manager dashboard. Check Create rota, Open rotas, Time tracking and refresh are on one row. Activate each, return, and check 768 and 1440 pixels.

All four actions are visible on one row without clipping, overlap or horizontal page scrolling at normal text size. Labels and focus indicators are readable and each action works. Desktop sizing remains correct.
Keep zone and status filters beside each other on narrow screens
Attendance enabled; employees across at least two zones and statuses; latest layout change deployed.
At 320, 348, 360 and 390 CSS pixels, inspect Today's team. Enter a name, choose a zone and status, then clear each filter. Repeat with long zone names and with attendance disabled.
All zones; All statuses; long zone label

Search has a readable full row. Zone and status share the next row without overflow and their combined filters return the correct employees. With attendance disabled the zone filter remains usable across the available width.
Refresh and resume update attendance without stale team rows
Manager dashboard open; second test account can clock in and out in staging.

Record current counts and team state. Clock the employee in from the second device. Refresh the dashboard, background and reopen it, then repeat after clock-out. Change location and date between checks.
Scheduled and unscheduled employee; two locations
Working and attention counts, team statuses and update time reflect the selected location and day. No duplicate employee rows or data from the previous location remain.
Attention request failure does not block the main dashboard
Release build; staging request interception for attention data only.
Open the dashboard with attention data delayed, then fail that request. Check main staffing data and navigation. Restore the request and use the available refresh or retry control.
Core dashboard content and actions remain usable. Attention loading or failure is visible and recoverable. Failure is not displayed as a healthy zero count.
Optimised dashboard queries respect manager location access
One manager limited to location A; location B has distinct employee data.
Open the dashboard and location selector as the restricted manager. Try a bookmarked dashboard or request for location B, then return to A. Repeat as an employee.
Two locations; restricted manager and employee
Only authorised locations, staff and attendance are returned. Employee access does not expose the manager dashboard or management actions.
Dashboard remains useful when attendance is disabled
Location with published shifts and attendance disabled; authorised manager.
Open the dashboard directly and navigate to it from another route. Change date and zone, inspect team rows and try rota actions.
Published staffing is shown correctly. Attendance-only controls and statuses are omitted, filters remain usable, and no clock data access error prevents the dashboard loading.
Open the deferred manual clock dialog on first and repeat use
Authorised clock manager; staging location with eligible employees.
Load Time tracking with network recording. Open manual clock override, close without submitting, and reopen. In a separate run fail the dialog chunk request and exercise the error recovery.
First open; repeat open; chunk load failure

Page loads without downloading the heavy form before it is needed. First open provides a loading state then a usable form, repeat open works, and load failure is recoverable without recording attendance.
Backdated manual clocking uses location time and rejects invalid chronology
Staging manager; location timezone differs from device; employee with known clock history.

Submit a valid backdated manual clock-in/out with a reason. Verify stored and displayed times. Attempt a future time, an out before its in, and a backdate conflicting with a later entry. Repeat at an overnight or DST boundary.
Europe/London DST boundary; different device timezone
Valid times use the location timezone and appear consistently in dashboard and timesheets. Invalid or conflicting chronology is rejected with no partial or duplicate entry.
Overdue scheduled entry closes as an estimate requiring review
Staging scheduled open time entry; known location reminder and hard-review thresholds; background job enabled.
Observe the entry before and after its scheduled end plus hard-review threshold. Run the processor again. Inspect dashboard, timesheet, estimated finish, note and clock event.
Published scheduled shift; custom hard-review delay

Entry stays open before the threshold, then closes at its estimated scheduled finish rather than job processing time. It requires manager review and is labelled as estimated. Repeated processing creates no duplicate closure or audit event.
Unscheduled closure uses the selected location's configured limit
Staging unscheduled open entries at two locations with different configured limits.
Check reminder timing and text at each location. Advance processing to each configured limit and process twice. Inspect payable duration, estimated finish and review status.
Different unscheduled limits and reminder lead times
Each entry uses its own location limit and reminder wording. Closure estimates the finish from clock-in plus that limit, never gives negative duration, and requires review without duplicates.
Clock-out reminder does not notify an employee who has already finished
Staging reminder eligible entry; controlled processor and employee clock-out timing.
Claim a due reminder, clock the employee out before dispatch, then resume dispatch. In separate runs simulate a push provider failure and no subscribed device.
Clock-out before dispatch; push failure; no device
Closed entries receive no stale reminder. Push failure does not block automatic closure or falsely record delivery. Entries with no subscribed devices do not retry indefinitely.
Use 12-hour and 24-hour time consistently across attendance pages
Manager and employee accounts; entries at midnight, noon and overnight.
Select each supported time format in settings. Inspect dashboard shifts, Time tracking, manual clock forms and timesheets. Reload and compare with a device in another timezone.
Supported displays follow the saved location preference without changing the underlying timestamps, durations or location date. Noon and midnight remain unambiguous.
Draft saves do not increment the visible publication number
Staging rota with an initial publication and employee viewer.
Publish the draft and note its visible publication number. Edit and save twice without republishing. Check employee view, then republish once and check visible number and unread indicator.
Multiple draft saves between two publications
Visible publication number changes only when a new publication is made. Employee sees the previous snapshot until republish, then the new publication and appropriate unread state.
Time-clock feature flags apply per location and are enforced server-side
Staging admin; locations A and B; authorised clock manager; independent clock-in and clock-out flags.

Disable clock-in at A while leaving B enabled. Wait for flag cache expiry, reload each page and attempt the corresponding request directly. Repeat for the clock-out flag, restore defaults and verify recovery.
Two locations; clock-in and clock-out flag variants
Disabled actions fail server-side only for the targeted location. Other enabled actions and locations continue to work. Re-enabling restores access after refresh without losing existing attendance.
Disabled shift swaps cannot be used through a bookmarked route
Staging workspace with rota access; shift-swap availability flag configurable.
Disable shift swaps and open /app/<workspaceSlug>/shift-swaps directly. Try a saved mutation request. Enable the feature and reload, then repeat as a user without rota access.
Disabled route gives a clear unavailable state and mutations are blocked. Enabled authorised users receive the working flow. Users without access remain denied regardless of flag state.
Manager announcement targeting stays within managed locations
Manager limited to A; owner; employees assigned only to A or B.

Publish a staging announcement to A and inspect each employee account. As manager try targeting B or the entire organisation. As owner test valid organisation-wide targeting. Archive the test announcement.
Only intended employees receive or see the announcement. Manager cannot target unmanaged locations or organisation-wide scope. Owner's permitted organisation target works.
Announcement notification preferences persist without hiding in-app content
Test employee subscribed to push; preference controls available; test announcement author.

Change the supported announcement notification preference and reload. Send one staging announcement with notifications enabled and another after disabling that category. Inspect in-app unread state and push delivery, then restore the preference.

Saved preference persists and supported notification channels respect it. Targeted announcements remain readable in-app. Reading an announcement clears its unread state without creating duplicate notifications.
First use of create-rota and template dialogs works after route splitting
Staging manager; location with zones and saved template; release build.

Cold-load the rota list, open Create rota and create a disposable future draft. Open the template dialog for the first time, apply a known template with required confirmation, close and reopen. Check keyboard focus and loading feedback.
Dialogs load with feedback and restore focus on close. Location, week and template selections remain correct and actions save once without a blank modal or missing module error.
